subject: PMO: Token economics mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@fintechinc.com>, Drew Chen <cloud-partner@acmeplatform.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: PMO: Token economics mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers

Jamie / Drew —

Great talking earlier. Quick recap from my side and a few asks so we can convert the discovery into a marketplace private offer that matches FinTech Inc.'s procurement needs.

Summary from call:
- Primary use: user-facing summaries and embeddings for search (average context ~1,200 tokens, responses ~180 tokens).
- Current monthly consumption estimate from FinTech: ~1.6B tokens (Q4 peak 2.2B).
- Budget band mentioned on-call: $60k–$120k / month (procurement asked for an annualized view).

What we need to map next (asks):
1) Procurement to confirm target $/1M tokens that would make the PO viable for Finance (give us a floor/ceiling).
2) Any constraints on invoice structure (line-item vs unit price vs committed spend).
3) Confirmation of which marketplace you want the private offer on (AWS vs GCP vs Azure) — we can create equivalent private offers across clouds but pricing mechanics differ.

Attached: FinTech usage export (Q4 2025) to help model monthly smoothing and burst. I’ve flagged the rows we discussed.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal: map hosted list prices to expected private-offer unit price for each cloud (Jonas to run a short model).
- External: Procurement provides target $/1M tokens and preferred marketplace by EOD Tue (1/13).

If you want, we can run a short joint call (30 min) next week to sign off the rate card before procurement issues a PO.

Thanks — feel free to ping me directly if there’s anything sensitive you don’t want in the thread.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[aisha.rahman@redwood.ai]
[attachment: fintech_usage_Q4_2025.csv (csv, 82KB)]

From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@fintechinc.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PMO: Token economics mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers

Aisha —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from procurement/finance before we get to private-offer specifics:

1) Our finance team wants an initial target unit we can present: at commit size ~1.6B tokens/mo, what is Redwood's suggested $/1M tokens for a 12mo committed PO on AWS private offer? We need a single number to run through our approval path.
2) How does a private offer unit map to your hosted API unit? Is it identical (e.g., $X per 1M tokens) or are there marketplace fees that change the math?
3) For invoicing: we prefer a single monthly invoice against a PO number with unit pricing; is that supported?

High-level budget guidance from FinTech: our procurement lead would like a target unit that gives us ~30–40% uplift over current internal compute cost but keeps vendor spend within the $60k–$120k range you noted.

We can provide our internal cost-per-token estimate privately if needed. Also looped in Drew from our cloud partner (cc) to confirm any marketplace-handling specifics on the AWS side.

Would appreciate a short written mapping back (hosted list price -> marketplace list -> private-offer unit) so we can forward to Finance.

—
Jamie Ortiz
Head of Procurement
FinTech Inc.
[jamie.ortiz@fintechinc.com]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@fintechinc.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PMO: Token economics mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers

Jamie / Aisha —

I pulled a concise mapping and attached a rate matrix (rate_matrix.xlsx) plus a draft PO terms doc (draft_aws_po_terms.docx) you can share with Finance. Key points below — this is a short model (happy to walk through numbers on a call).

Assumptions:
- Baseline hosted API list price we currently publish (example model for text-gen + embedding blended): $22.00 / 1M tokens.
- Marketplace listing fees/handling approximate delta: AWS marketplace listing + AWS fees typically add ~6–9% on top of our hosted list price for published listing, which we absorb when necessary for parity. Private offers allow direct unit renegotiation.

Indicative private-offer mappings (annual 12-mo commit; volumes ~1.6B tokens/mo):
- Hosted list price: $22.00 / 1M tokens
- AWS marketplace list (catalog equivalent): ~$23.50 / 1M tokens (includes catalogue processing margin)
- Proposed private-offer unit (target to present to Finance): $16.50 / 1M tokens (this equates to ~25% below hosted list; gives FinTech ~30% uplift vs their internal compute band mentioned on call)

Price band sensitivity (for modeling):
- If FinTech targets $20k / month (low end): unit would need to land ~ $36.00 / 1M to fit — not feasible for their scale.
- For $60k–$120k / month (the band on call): at 1.6B tokens/mo -> effective required unit ranges approximately $37.5 -> $75 per 1M tokens, which suggests your stated budget is inconsistent with the 1.6B figure if interpreted as 'vendor spend' rather than internal compute.

Two ways to reconcile:
1) Confirm tokens: is 1.6B tokens "billable Redwood tokens" (i.e., what we'd meter) or an internal estimate that includes client-side compute? If the latter, actual vendor-billed tokens may be lower.
2) Commit to a tiered pricing schedule in the private offer: e.g., $18 / 1M for first 200M, $16 / 1M for 200M–2.0B, and $14 / 1M over 2.0B — plus a minimum monthly commitment to meet Finance thresholds. This structure can bring vendor spend into the $60k–$120k band while preserving unit economics.

Attachments: rate_matrix.xlsx (sample per-cloud mapping + a simple model), draft_aws_po_terms.docx (standard private-offer language, editable).

Action items (proposal):
- FinTech: confirm whether 1.6B is Redwood-metered tokens or an internal metric.
- FinTech: suggest a concrete target $/1M tokens (single number or band) by EOD Tue (1/13) so we can produce a formal private-offer draft.
- Redwood (Jonas): prepare a formal private-offer price sheet for AWS + optional equivalents for GCP/Azure once target is confirmed.

Happy to schedule a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow (1/13) to present the matrix — Aisha to coordinate if that helps.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.ai]
[attachment: rate_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)]
[attachment: draft_aws_po_terms.docx (docx, 28KB)]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@fintechinc.com>, Drew Chen <cloud-partner@acmeplatform.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PMO: Token economics mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers — next steps

Jamie / Drew —

Thanks for the quick replies and for looping Drew in. Short checklist to keep momentum:

1) Procurement confirmation: Please reply with either a single target $/1M tokens or a band we should use in the draft PO (example suggested by Jonas: $16.50 / 1M as an anchor).
2) Token accounting: If you can send a short note confirming whether the 1.6B includes client-side pre/post-processing tokens (or is Redwood-metered), we’ll rerun the model.
3) PO mechanics: Confirm preferred marketplace (AWS preferred per Drew) and whether monthly single-invoice against PO number works. We support monthly unit billing tied to PO number.

If we get the confirmation today, Jonas will produce a clean private-offer draft (AWS) and I’ll work with our contracts team to get the DocuSign-ready PO wrapper by EOD Thursday (1/15).

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes on Wed 1/14 at 10:00 PT to review the rate matrix and sign the approach. Let me know if that works for you and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — appreciate the speed here.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
